title: Austria still requires routine noise-declaration copies
statusLabel: Deletion proposed; current copy clause remains
deadlineLabel: EU application date; adoption/publication due 28 November 2025
summary: A government draft proposes removing the copy duty, but the published regulation still contains it.
nationalGap: Section 6(3) requires manufacturers or representatives to send a declaration copy to the Commission and competent Member State authority. For Austria it names the ministry. The 2026 draft would delete this paragraph.
nationalLaw: BGBl. II No 249/2001, as amended through No 347/2006
consequence: Yes, on paper: a routine submission duty remains. Whether it is still enforced or must be disapplied requires legal review.
resolution: Draft point 8 would remove Section 6(3). No later enacted deletion was located in the current regulation or official Gazette API search on 26 October 2026.
caveat: The copy clause states no prior-submission deadline; no premarketing condition, automatic fine or actual filing burden is inferred. Declaration preparation, ten-year retention and reasoned market-surveillance requests remain separate. EU primacy or consistent interpretation may protect operators. The Commission procedure concerns implementation notification and does not decide this specific clause’s legality.

comparison.before: Routine copies to Commission and Member State authority.
comparison.note: Retention and targeted requests are distinct.

review: Independent current-law, government-draft and adverse-scope reviews passed. Official Gazette API title and implementing-reference searches checked for later enactment; practical enforcement remains unverified.
recognitionNote: Government explanatory point 8 identifies the exact repeal. The Commission’s implementation procedure is broader and does not specifically adjudicate Section 6(3).
